text: Three of Elena's six symptoms get traced to their actual root causes here: the AP aging mismatch, the AR confusion on Harborview's account, and the heavy depreciation number. Nothing gets fixed yet — this lesson is pure investigation.

AP: checking account 2150 for Company 1000 shows two entries for the same PO — December's GRNI journal and January's validated invoice, both $18,400. The GL's accrued liability is $18,400 too high because the December accrual never reversed.

AR: pulling Harborview's aging by invoice instead of total balance shows it immediately — one invoice overdue, another sitting on a forty-nine-thousand-dollar credit. The receipt application history confirms RCPT-50231 was applied to the wrong invoice entirely.

Assets: FA-10452's record shows Office Equipment, five-year life, cost center 410. The capital approval paperwork for a CNC lathe confirms it should be Manufacturing Equipment, ten-year life, cost center 420 — exactly the mismatch planted when it was capitalized.
Three root causes confirmed with evidence, nothing corrected yet. Up next, lesson twenty: investigating Cash Management, Subledger Accounting, and General Ledger — the remaining three symptoms.
